notes: Controlled vocabulary for cinematography metadata. Every value used in library/cinema-metadata.json must appear here. 'basis' says how a dimension is filled: 'measured' values are computed from the image pixels by tools/measure-stills.js and can be regenerated at any time; 'observed' values are read from the image by a viewer and describe only what is visible; 'interpretation' values are subjective and are never mixed into the other two. 'multi' dimensions take a list. Terms can be added freely; never rename a published term, add a new one and migrate instead. Definitions double as the glossary shown with Taste Profile findings. 'groups' in a dimension define broader terms derived from its values (e.g. close shots = medium close-up, close-up or extreme close-up); the engine adds them automatically, so rare values can still be detected together.

key.label: tonal key
key.definition: Where most of the image's tones sit between black and white.

low.label: low-key
low.definition: Most of the frame is dark; light is selective and shadows dominate.

mid.label: mid-key
mid.definition: Tones are spread around the middle greys; neither shadow nor light dominates.

high.label: high-key
high.definition: Most of the frame is bright; shadows are few and light.

contrast.label: contrast
contrast.definition: The spread between the darkest and brightest significant tones.

low.label: low contrast
low.definition: A narrow tonal range; soft, compressed blacks and whites.

high.label: high contrast
high.definition: A wide tonal range from deep blacks to bright highlights.

monochrome.label: monochrome
monochrome.definition: Black and white, or a toned print (sepia, blue) with a single tint and no colour variety.

muted.label: muted colour
muted.definition: Desaturated colour; greys and earth tones dominate.

toned.label: toned print
toned.definition: A monochrome image carrying a single tint, such as sepia.

yes.label: toned print
yes.definition: A black-and-white image printed or tinted in one colour, such as sepia.

temperature.label: colour temperature
temperature.definition: Whether the overall colour leans towards orange (warm) or blue (cool).

warm.label: warm
warm.definition: The image leans towards amber, orange or red.

neutral.label: neutral
neutral.definition: No strong lean towards warm or cool, or an untoned black-and-white image.

cool.label: cool
cool.definition: The image leans towards blue, teal or green.

hue.label: dominant hues
hue.definition: The hue families that cover a significant share of the coloured pixels.

harmony.label: colour harmony
harmony.definition: How the colours present relate on the colour wheel. Not recorded for monochrome images.

single-hue.label: single-hue palette
single-hue.definition: One hue family dominates the coloured areas (three quarters or more).

analogous.label: analogous palette
analogous.definition: Neighbouring hues, such as red, orange and yellow, share the frame.

contrasting.label: contrasting palette
contrasting.definition: Hues from opposite sides of the wheel, such as orange against blue, share the frame.

accent.label: colour accent
accent.definition: A small area of vivid colour in an otherwise dark or muted frame.

yes.label: colour accent
yes.definition: A small vivid area (between half a percent and 8% of the frame) stands out against a muted or dark image.

symmetry.label: tonal symmetry
symmetry.definition: How closely the brightness of the left half mirrors the right half. Measured from tone only, not from shapes or arrangement: a dark, even frame can score high. Arranged symmetry is the observed composition term 'symmetrical composition'.

strong.label: strong tonal symmetry
strong.definition: The brightness of the two halves nearly mirrors.

moderate.label: partial tonal symmetry
moderate.definition: The halves are broadly balanced in brightness but not mirrored.

weak.label: tonal asymmetry
weak.definition: The halves differ clearly in brightness and mass.

detail.label: surface detail
detail.definition: How much fine edge detail and texture the image carries, measured as average local gradient.

smooth.label: smooth
smooth.definition: Large even areas with few edges.

moderate.label: moderate detail
moderate.definition: A mix of even areas and textured ones.

dense.label: dense detail
dense.definition: Busy surfaces, many edges and fine texture across the frame.

medium.label: medium
medium.definition: How the image was made, as visible in the frame.

live-action.label: live action
live-action.definition: Photographed with a camera (including sets, models and miniatures).

lightQuality.label: light quality
lightQuality.definition: Whether shadows have sharp or gradual edges.

hard.label: hard light
hard.definition: Crisp, sharp-edged shadows from a small or distant source.

soft.label: soft light
soft.definition: Gradual shadow edges from a large or diffused source.

mixed.label: mixed light
mixed.definition: Both hard and soft light are clearly present.

lightDirection.label: key-light direction
lightDirection.definition: The apparent direction of the main light on the subject.

front.label: frontal light
front.definition: Light from near the camera, flattening form.

side.label: side light
side.definition: Light from one side, modelling form with shadow.

back.label: backlight
back.definition: Light from behind the subject, rimming or silhouetting it.

top.label: top light
top.definition: Light from above, shadowing eyes and lower forms.

ambient.label: ambient light
ambient.definition: No single directional source; light is even or diffuse.

lightSource.label: apparent light source
lightSource.definition: What appears to light the scene, judged from the image only. 'practical' requires the source to be visible in the frame. Left undetermined when the image does not show it.

practical.label: practical light
practical.definition: Visible lamps, fire, candles, screens or signs within the frame.

artificial.label: artificial light
artificial.definition: Electric light from sources outside the frame.

mixed.label: mixed sources
mixed.definition: Daylight and artificial or practical light together.

shotScale.label: shot scale
shotScale.definition: How much of the subject and its surroundings the frame includes.

extreme-wide.label: extreme wide shot
extreme-wide.definition: Figures are tiny or absent; the setting dominates.

full.label: full shot
full.definition: A figure from head to feet filling most of the frame height.

medium.label: medium shot
medium.definition: Figures from about the waist up.

close-up.label: close-up
close-up.definition: A face or object fills most of the frame.

extreme-close-up.label: extreme close-up
extreme-close-up.definition: A detail such as eyes or a hand fills the frame.

close-range.label: close shots
close-range.definition: Any shot from medium close-up to extreme close-up: the frame is mostly face, body or object.

distant.label: distant shots
distant.definition: Wide and extreme wide shots: the setting dominates the figures.

angle.label: camera angle
angle.definition: The apparent camera height and tilt relative to the subject.

eye-level.label: eye level
eye-level.definition: The camera is at about the subject's eye height.

high.label: high angle
high.definition: The camera looks down on the subject.

low.label: low angle
low.definition: The camera looks up at the subject.

off-level.label: high or low camera
off-level.definition: Any angle other than eye level: high, low, overhead or canted.

composition.label: composition
composition.definition: Visible devices that organise the frame.

centred.label: centred subject
centred.definition: The main subject sits on the vertical centre line.

off-centre.label: off-centre subject
off-centre.definition: The main subject is placed clearly to one side.

symmetrical.label: symmetrical composition
symmetrical.definition: The frame is arranged to mirror around its centre.

leading-lines.label: leading lines
leading-lines.definition: Lines in the set or landscape draw the eye towards a point.

frame-within-frame.label: frame within a frame
frame-within-frame.definition: A doorway, window or other shape frames the subject inside the image.

negative-space.label: negative space
negative-space.definition: Large empty areas surround the subject.

diagonal.label: diagonal composition
diagonal.definition: Strong diagonal lines or placements organise the frame.

staging-in-depth.label: staging in depth
staging-in-depth.definition: Figures or objects are placed at clearly different distances from the camera.

foreground-framing.label: foreground framing
foreground-framing.definition: Out-of-focus or dark objects in the foreground edge the frame.

dense.label: dense composition
dense.definition: The frame is filled with many figures or objects.

silhouette.label: silhouette
silhouette.definition: Subjects appear as dark shapes against a brighter background.

lightPattern.label: light pattern
lightPattern.definition: Visible shapes the light makes in the frame.

patterned-shadow.label: patterned shadow
patterned-shadow.definition: Shadows cast through blinds, bars, lattices or leaves stripe or dapple the scene.

pools.label: pools of light
pools.definition: Isolated areas of light surrounded by darkness.

rim.label: rim light
rim.definition: A bright edge of light outlines a figure or object against a darker background.

beams.label: visible beams
beams.definition: Shafts or beams of light are visible in the air.

glare.label: glare
glare.definition: A light source shines towards the lens: flare, bloom or a blazing lamp.

even.label: even light
even.definition: None of these: the light falls without distinct shapes.

shaped.label: shaped light
shaped.definition: Light that makes visible shapes: pools, beams, rim light, glare or patterned shadow.

atmospherics.label: atmospherics
atmospherics.definition: What is visible in the air between camera and subject.

mist.label: mist or haze
mist.definition: Fog, mist or haze softens distance.

smoke.label: smoke
smoke.definition: Smoke or steam drifts in the frame.

veiled.label: veiled air
veiled.definition: Something in the air between camera and subject: mist, smoke, rain or dust.

gaze.label: gaze
gaze.definition: Where the main figure is looking.

camera.label: gaze at the camera
camera.definition: The main figure looks into or very near the lens.

within.label: gaze within the frame
within.definition: The main figure looks at someone or something visible in the frame.

off-frame.label: gaze out of frame
off-frame.definition: The main figure looks at something outside the frame.

averted.label: averted or downcast gaze
averted.definition: The main figure looks down or away, inward.

hidden.label: face not visible
hidden.definition: The main figure's face is turned away, hidden or too small to read.

still.label: stillness
still.definition: Figures and objects are at rest.

implied.label: implied motion
implied.definition: A figure or object is caught mid-movement.

focus.label: depth of field
focus.definition: How much of the scene, front to back, appears sharp. Recorded only when the frame contains planes at clearly different distances; otherwise left undetermined (the flatness of a scene is described by spatial layers instead).

shallow.label: shallow focus
shallow.definition: Only one plane is sharp; the rest is soft.

deep.label: deep focus
deep.definition: Near and far planes are both sharp.

layers.label: spatial layers
layers.definition: How many distinct planes of depth the frame shows.

one.label: single plane
one.definition: Subject and background read as one plane.

two.label: two planes
two.definition: A subject plane and a distinct background.

three-plus.label: three or more planes
three-plus.definition: Foreground, middle ground and background are all distinct.

figures.label: figures
figures.definition: How many people, or human-like characters in animation, the frame shows.

setting.label: setting
setting.definition: Whether the scene is indoors or outdoors.

vehicle.label: vehicle
vehicle.definition: Inside a car, train, spacecraft or other vehicle.

atmosphere.label: atmosphere
atmosphere.definition: A subjective reading of the mood the image creates. Recorded separately and never treated as an observed fact.

thresholds.notes: Cut-points for measured dimensions, applied by tools/measure-stills.js. Luminance and saturation are 0–1 on sRGB values. Changing a threshold and re-running the tool regenerates every measured value; nothing else changes.

saturation.metric: mean HSV saturation of pixels brighter than 0.08

hue.metric: share of saturated pixels (S > 0.2, V > 0.15) in each hue family

symmetry.metric: 1 - mean |L(x) - L(mirror x)| / mean |L(x) - L(x shifted half a frame)|, on a 64-px-wide luminance map; 1 = mirrored, about 0 = no more alike than unrelated areas

toned.metric: circular standard deviation of hue (degrees) over coloured pixels; a toned print is monochrome with a single tint, and keeps its temperature

detail.metric: mean Sobel gradient magnitude on a 256-px luminance map

accent.metric: share of vivid pixels (S > 0.55, V > 0.3) with mean saturation below a limit

retired.focus:flat: 2026-10-21: mixed depth of field with the depth of the scene; those stills are now 'undetermined' for focus, and spatial layers carry the flatness.
retired.atmosphere:nostalgic: 2026-10-21: depended on knowing a film's period rather than on the image.
